program.name: ndm_pca
program.help:
Compute principal component analysis (PCA).
PARAMETERS
All mandatory parameters are defined in the 'Acquisition System' and 'Spike Groups' tab.
OPTIONAL PARAMETERS
# before
Number of samples before the peak to use for the PCA. This can be either a space-separated list of numbers (one per electrode group), or a single common number for all groups.
# after
Number of samples after the peak to use for the PCA. This can be either a space-separated list of numbers (one per electrode group), or a single common number for all groups.
# extra
Whether extra features (spike peak value) should be included in the output files.
# varimax
Apply a Varimax rotation to each channel's kept PCA components before projection (default false). Total explained variance is unchanged, but each rotated component tends to localise on a few waveform samples, which can make cluster structure easier to read during manual sorting. The rotation is baked into the saved .pca basis, so all downstream tools (including Klusters reprojection) follow it automatically. Applies to standard and stderiv methods alike.
# varimaxMaxIter
Maximum number of Varimax rotation sweeps (default 30). Only used when varimax is enabled.
# varimaxTol
Relative change in the Varimax criterion at which the rotation is considered converged (default 1e-6). Only used when varimax is enabled. METHOD TOKENS
The method may be qualified so the transform is stated in the artifact name rather than inferred: stderiv_S<order> runs the plain spatial derivative (orders 1-3) and leaves any per-group sdiffPairs unused, while stderiv_C<order> applies the session's sdiffPairs pattern -- order 4 for a single-partner pattern, order 5 for a reference-set pattern (one written with '+'). Outputs are stamped with the full token, e.g. <session>.spk.stderiv_C4.<group>.
Orders 4 and 5 are derived from the pattern itself and cannot be requested through methodOrder; a plain "stderiv" keeps the historical behaviour of applying whatever sdiffPairs the groups define.
# featureLag
0 (or absent) selects the classic per-channel feature space: PC1, PC2, PC3.
A non-zero N selects the lag feature space that fiber-session builds under --feat-lag N, and which its artifacts name with a _D<lag><dims> suffix -- a session emitted as stderiv_C5_D34 is _C5 for the custom sdiffPairs pattern and _D34 for lag 3, 4 dimensions. Each channel then contributes PC1 sampled at -N/0/+N samples plus PC2: FOUR columns instead of three, and unlike PC1,PC2,PC3 they are not orthogonal.
Per group, like nFeatures, because a group can be re-featurised on its own and the two describe the same thing -- the width and the meaning of a channel's feature block.
# dropLastChannel
The spatial derivative leaves one channel that the reduction drops before PCA, so a group of N channels normally yields N-1. For orders 1 and 3 that channel is an exact linear combination of the others and the drop costs nothing. For a custom sdiffPairs pattern (methods stderiv_C4 / stderiv_C5) the transform may be full rank, and because PCA is fit PER CHANNEL and truncated to nFeatures, the dropped channel's features are not exactly reproducible from the kept ones.
Set false to keep every channel (N features groups instead of N-1). The basis records the width it was fit at, so ndm_refeaturize reads THIS node's value rather than its own and downstream readers follow the basis. Changing it invalidates existing .fet/.pca for the session -- refit rather than mixing widths. Default true.
